finding.claim: SQL injection in /search. The q query parameter is interpolated into the SQL string with an f-string. An unauthenticated attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION SELECT queries to read any table in shop.db, such as users or credentials. sqlite3's execute() rejects stacked statements, so the attack is limited to reads and injected subqueries.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes the raw user input with no validation
term is formatted directly into the SQL text instead of being bound as a parameter
Query results are returned as JSON, so UNION-based injection exfiltrates data directly in the response

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping or allow-list on term. No authentication or authorization decorators on the route. No WAF or middleware in app.py. The other two routes use parameterized queries (lines 18 and 25), but this one does not.

verdict.reason: app.py:11-12 takes request.args 'q' and interpolates it into the LIKE literal in an f-string with no validation, auth or parameterization, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so UNION SELECT output is returned directly (the other routes at lines 18 and 25 are parameterized, as claimed).

verdict_facts.reason: app.py:11-13 reads q from request.args and interpolates it into the LIKE query via an f-string at app.py:12. The route has no auth decorator, validation or parameter binding, and the result is returned as JSON at app.py:13, so UNION-based reads work.
